props.name: render
props.description: Replaces the host `<h2>` via base-ui `useRender`. Use this for other outline levels; the level-2 type classes and `data-slot` stay merged onto the replacement.

props.name: layout
props.description: How each Item's terms and details sit. `responsive` stacks the details under the term on phones and sets them in two columns from `sm` up, with a rule between Items at every width. `inline` is for label/value rows in cards and summaries: each Item shares its own row between its term and details, whatever the other Items hold. The details sits at the end of the term's line while the two fit, and the term wraps beside it until its longest word would not fit; then the details moves under the term, end-aligned, and wraps only when it is wider than the row. Inline rows take the label type, have no rules and space with the small surface gap, and the term is not muted. A colour class on a cell wins in both layouts. The inline cells' padding, sizing and alignment come from the list, so override them with a `[:where([data-layout=inline]>*)>&]:` class or a CSS rule, and an inline Item's row, wrap and gap with a `[:where([data-layout=inline])>&]:` class. Defaults to `responsive`.
